name: GlobalFoundries

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (GF logo horz rgb R 2025.svg)

description: GlobalFoundries is a contract chip maker: it runs four wafer fabs (Malta NY, Burlington VT, Dresden Germany, Singapore) and manufactures chips designed by other companies. It does not chase the smallest transistor sizes; it sells specialty processes (low-power, RF, power, silicon photonics, embedded memory) mostly into cars, phones, industrial and IoT devices, and communications gear. Customers pay per wafer, with some long-term agreements that include minimum-volume or underutilization payments, plus a small non-wafer stream of licensing and engineering fees (11% of 2025 revenue) that it is growing by buying processor-IP businesses (MIPS in 2025, Synopsys's ARC unit agreed in 2026). Abu Dhabi's Mubadala owns about 81%, and US and New York subsidies and a US Commerce Department equity deal fund its US expansion.

hq.note: Principal executive offices 400 Stonebreak Road Extension, Malta, NY (FY2025 20-F); incorporated in the Cayman Islands in October 2008

employees.note: "approximately 14,000 employees primarily located at our manufacturing sites"; about 1,600 in R&D (FY2025 20-F)

businessLines.name: Smart Mobile Devices
businessLines.how: Wafers sold per unit to chip designers with cost and power as the buying criteria; short design and qualification cycles.
businessLines.description: Chips for smartphones, tablets and wearables: RF front-end, connectivity, sensors, power management, audio.

businessLines.name: Automotive
businessLines.how: Wafers sold per unit under long-lifetime, high-reliability qualifications, often locked in for years once a chip is designed into a car platform.
businessLines.description: ADAS radar front-ends, signal processing, EV and hybrid power management, in-vehicle networking, body control, infotainment.

businessLines.name: Home and Industrial IoT
businessLines.how: Wafers sold per unit for long-life, extended-temperature, ultra-low-power chips; also trusted and secure manufacturing for defense customers.
businessLines.description: Connected home, industrial automation, building and energy management, edge AI sensing, plus aerospace and defense including radiation-hardened parts.

businessLines.name: Communications Infrastructure and Data Center
businessLines.how: Wafers sold per unit for RF, timing and optical-modulator chips where bandwidth and power efficiency decide the process choice.
businessLines.description: Wireless and wireline infrastructure, optical networks, satellite communications and data center interconnect, including silicon photonics.

businessLines.name: Non-wafer revenue
businessLines.how: Customers pay license fees and one-off engineering charges for design work and technology access, separate from per-wafer pricing.
businessLines.description: Licensing fees, non-recurring engineering (NRE) services and, from 2025, processor IP (MIPS).
